transcript:
Header: 2026-07-09 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Liam Patel (Sequoia), Hannah Kim (Sequoia), Omar Ruiz (Sequoia)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're excited to show the Console usage analytics and per-route cost breakdown today. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE, and Diego's our SE.
[00:12] Liam Patel: Hey Maya, thanks. I'm Liam — will be running platform evals here. Hannah and Omar are on too.
[00:18] Hannah Kim: Hi all.
[00:21] Diego Alvarez: Quick agenda: demo the per-route dashboards, show token-level cost attribution, latency p50/p95/p99, call out troubleshooting views (traces, sample requests), and how Optimize recommends batching/quantization to lower cost.
[00:36] Omar Ruiz: Sounds good. Our main constraints: interactive chat widget p95 under 200ms, nightly batch embeds are fine up to minutes, and we need EU data residency for some customers.
[00:49] Maya Chen: Great — we'll flag where Dedicated or Private helps with residency.
[00:54] Diego Alvarez: Jumping in — opening the Console. Top-left is global usage: total tokens, calls, cost burn by day. You can filter by model, environment, and team.
[01:10] Diego Alvarez: Now per-route view — this is where we map API routes (like /v1/generate-chat or /v1/embeddings) to business labels. You can see call volume, avg tokens in/out, cost per call, and cost per 1k calls.
[01:27] Hannah Kim: Quick question — how do you map our internal route names? Will we need to add tags server-side?
[01:33] Diego Alvarez: Two options: automatic mapping via path heuristics, or you can attach metadata in the request header (x-redwood-route) for exact attribution. Many customers use middleware to set route tags.
[01:45] Liam Patel: Is that header encrypted in logs or can you opt out? We have PII concerns.
[01:51] Diego Alvarez: The header is only used for attribution, not stored in plain text in analytics export by default; you can mask or hash values and still get aggregated metrics. We'll share the docs on metadata handling.
[02:05] Maya Chen: Also, for Private deployments you can disable analytics export entirely and keep logs in your own S3 or logging stack.
[02:15] Omar Ruiz: Good. Show us cost breakdown for our chat widget route.
[02:19] Diego Alvarez: Here — route 'chat-widget' selected. You can see: tokens in, tokens out, avg latency, p50/p95/p99, and cost attribution. Note the cost column is split into model compute, KV cache hits (savings), and infra overhead.
[02:36] Diego Alvarez: See this spike on June 24th? If you drill into traces, we show sample requests and where latency came from — e.g., model cold start, network to VPC endpoint, or post-processing.
[02:49] Hannah Kim: The KV cache thing — can Redwood share what counts as a cache hit? We run prefix caching on some long conversations.
[02:56] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we track KV cache hits when the model reuses past k-v states in the request lifecycle; hits reduce token generation and show up as separate line items in the cost view. Sometimes transcripts show 'cache mismatch' when session IDs differ.
[03:12] Liam Patel: How accurate is the per-route cost? We need granularity to chargeback to product teams.
[03:18] Maya Chen: Per-route cost is modeled from token-level accounting and kernel/runtime selection. For Hosted it's accurate within a few percent; Dedicated gives tighter fidelity since you can pin model variants and kernel profiles. We'll include a short note on rounding/overheads in the docs.
[03:36] Omar Ruiz: Any visibility into model variant fallbacks? We sometimes route to cheaper variants when under pressure.
[03:43] Diego Alvarez: Yes — routing policies show which variant served a request, and you can aggregate cost by variant. The dashboard shows fallback events and the percent of requests affected.
[03:55] Hannah Kim: Can we export per-route daily CSVs for internal chargeback?
[03:59] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely — export CSV or push to S3. You can also configure daily webhooks to your billing system.
[04:08] Liam Patel: On benchmarking — if we run a POC, can Redwood run the benchmark in Dedicated? We want to see tail latency under production load.
[04:18] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can run POC on Dedicated for accurate latency and cost numbers. We'll need your traffic profile and a traffic generator. We can also run a hosted baseline first.
[04:30] Maya Chen: For the POC we typically do two routes: one interactive (chat), one high-throughput (embeddings). We'll measure p95/p99, token cost, and quality metrics you define.
[04:44] Hannah Kim: Quality metrics — are you able to replay our prompt sets and get model outputs so our teams can evaluate regressions?
[04:50] Diego Alvarez: Yep, Console's evals let you run prompt sets and diff outputs. We can tie regressions to rollouts and alert when quality dips below thresholds.
[05:03] Omar Ruiz: Security — we need details on key management and SSO.
[05:07] Maya Chen: Diego will share the KMS and SAML docs. We support BYOK with customer KMS in Dedicated/Private and SAML SSO with SCIM for user provisioning.
[05:18] Diego Alvarez: And audit logs are configurable; you can route them to your SIEM. For Private deployments we can keep logs entirely on-prem or in your VPC.
[05:29] Liam Patel: Any gotchas on quantization recommendations? Our models include proprietary finetunes.
[05:35] Diego Alvarez: Optimize will recommend quant profiles per model but flags compatibility with finetunes. For sensitive finetunes you can run a quality check before applying quantization. Quantization tradeoffs are in the Optimize report.
[05:50] Hannah Kim: Can you show an example cost-savings scenario?
[05:54] Diego Alvarez: Sure — opening 'Optimize suggestions' tab. For embeddings-heavy route, batching + mixed-precision quantization reduced per-call cost by 42% in our benchmark. There's a before/after cost chart and estimated savings if you apply suggestions.
[06:12] Maya Chen: We also surface predicted ROI by simulating your historical traffic. If you connect usage for 30 days we can show expected monthly savings.
[06:22] Liam Patel: Ok that would be helpful. We'll probably want the 30-day sim before committing to Dedicated.
[06:29] Diego Alvarez: No problem. We'll need a sample of your logs — anonymized is fine.
[06:33] Omar Ruiz: About data residency — we have EU-only customers. Does Redwood host EU regions?
[06:38] Maya Chen: Yes, Hosted has EU regions; Dedicated can be provisioned in EU clouds and Private gives full control. We'll share the architecture note.
[06:46] Hannah Kim: Is there an SLA on latency or availability for Dedicated?
[06:50] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and target latency bands; we'll include those in the contract. Hosted has best-effort latency SLOs but Dedicated is the path for guaranteed p95 targets.
[07:01] Liam Patel: Great. A couple of adaptation questions: can dashboards be filtered by team or cost center?
[07:07] Diego Alvarez: Yes, you can attach route tags or team tags and filter dashboards. Chargeback exports include cost center fields.
[07:15] Hannah Kim: What about retrospective cost attribution if we rename routes?
[07:19] Diego Alvarez: We keep historical mappings and you can map aliases — but it's best practice to emit stable route identifiers to avoid gaps.
[07:28] Omar Ruiz: Any examples of customers who cut cost significantly?
[07:31] Maya Chen: We helped a fintech reduce inference spend 37% by batching embeddings and moving non-interactive workloads to a cheaper variant. We'll share a case study link.
[07:43] Liam Patel: Ok, this is helpful. Let's talk set-up timeline and POC steps.
[07:48] Maya Chen: Typical POC: data and traffic sample -> baseline hosted run -> Dedicated pilot -> results and ramp. Usually 2-4 weeks for initial runs depending on complexity.
[07:59] Hannah Kim: Our timeline: procurement for Q4, but we'd like to complete POC in July to make a decision.
[08:06] Maya Chen: Sounds doable. We'll aim to have pricing and docs to you within a few days.
[08:11] Diego Alvarez: I'll follow up with SOC2, KMS notes, and a short template for traffic sample.
[08:18] Liam Patel: Great. One last question — competitor differences: why Redwood vs Bedrock or Anthropic?
[08:24] Maya Chen: Short answer: developer-first runtime focused on production economics — per-route cost visibility, dedicated routing, and built-in Optimize recommendations. We'll send comparative notes.
[08:36] Hannah Kim: Thanks.
[08:37] Maya Chen: Ok recap and next steps — we'll send pricing spreadsheet, security docs, and schedule POC kickoff. Liam, Hannah, please share sample traffic and success criteria.
[08:48] Liam Patel: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[08:51] Omar Ruiz: Thanks.
[08:53] Diego Alvarez: Thanks team — we'll follow up.
